overview.description: Kothandaramar Temple is a Hindu temple located in the Tiruvarur district of Tamil Nadu, India, dedicated to Rama, the seventh avatar of the god Vishnu. The temple is glorified by Maharishi Valmiki and classified as one of the 108 Abhimana Kshethrams of the Vaishnavate tradition. This temple one of Pancha Rama Kshethrams. All these temples are said to be particular locations mentioned in Ramayana.
overview.about: Kothandaramar Temple in Thillaivilagam is an ancient and revered Hindu temple in Tiruvarur district, Tamil Nadu, dedicated to Lord Rama — the seventh avatar of Lord Vishnu. The temple is celebrated as one of the 108 Abhimana Kshethrams of Vaishnavism and is counted among the sacred Pancha Rama Kshethrams of the Cauvery delta region. Situated in a peaceful rural enclave near the Muthupet mangrove wetlands and Karpaganatharkulam, it features authentic Dravidian temple architecture, sacred theerthams, and vibrant Rama Navami traditions.

topPlaces.name: Kothandaramar Temple (Main Shrine)
topPlaces.description: The sacred principal shrine of Thillaivilagam, dedicated to Lord Kothandarama — Rama holding his divine bow (Kodhandam). Revered as one of the 108 Abhimana Kshethrams and among the sacred Pancha Rama Kshethrams glorified by Maharishi Valmiki in the Ramayana. The presiding deity stands majestically alongside Sita Devi and Lakshmana. The sanctum exudes profound spiritual tranquillity with traditional daily pujas, Ram Navami, and Panguni Uthiram celebrations.

image.alt: Kothandaramar Temple sanctum and temple premises — Thillaivilagam

topPlaces.name: Muthupet Mangrove Forest & Lagoon
topPlaces.description: Muthupet Lagoon is a stunning coastal mangrove wetland spanning over 6,900 hectares at the southern edge of the Cauvery delta. Famed for its dense Avicennia marina mangrove canopy, winding wooden boardwalks, and tidal waterways where fishermen navigate country boats. A paradise for nature lovers and birdwatchers observing flamingos, herons, and egrets during the winter migration.

image.alt: Dense mangroves and aerial pencil roots in Muthupet Lagoon

topPlaces.name: Karpaganathar Temple, Karpaganatharkulam
topPlaces.description: An ancient Chola-era Paadal Petra Sthalam Shiva temple located in nearby Karpaganatharkulam. Dedicated to Lord Karpaganathar (wish-fulfilling Shiva) and Goddess Balambikai. The temple features majestic multi-tiered gopurams, grand granite pillared halls, and the sacred Karpaga Theertham tank celebrated in Sangam literature and Tevaram hymns.

image.alt: Karpaganathar Temple main entrance and gopuram — Karpaganatharkulam

topPlaces.name: Sithamalli Sokkaayi Amman & Aiyanaar Temple
topPlaces.description: A historic rural heritage shrine in Sithamalli village near Muthupet, honoring Sokkaayi Amman and Lord Aiyanaar (Thiruvarasamoorthi). The temple exemplifies the traditional village folk deities and terracotta horse guardian art of the Cauvery delta, preserving centuries of agricultural community devotion and vibrant festive traditions.

image.alt: Chithamalli Aandavar Aiyanaar Temple front view — Sithamalli

topPlaces.name: Rajagopalaswamy Temple, Mannargudi
topPlaces.description: Known as Dakshina Dwaraka (Southern Dwaraka), this massive 10th-century Vaishnavite temple built by Chola king Kulothunga I is one of the most prominent shrines in Tiruvarur district. Spanning 23 acres with 16 grand gopurams, seven prakarams, and the colossal Haridra Nadhi temple tank — one of the largest in India.

topPlaces.name: Thyagaraja Temple & Kamalalayam, Thiruvarur
topPlaces.description: The monumental ancient temple complex of Lord Thyagaraja in Tiruvarur district capital, covering over 30 acres with 9 soaring gopurams and the world-famous colossal wooden temple chariot (Aazhi Ther). Adjoining the temple is Kamalalayam Lake, a 33-acre sacred reservoir with a central island shrine.
